scope: resolve the factor_pllvideo0x4_tbl size/range/endpoint conflict and prove the rate-selection behaviour of get_factors_pll_video0 for 286 MHz and 572 MHz

input_identity.relocation_overlay: in memory only, .rela.dyn addends; no relocated ELF written to disk

entry_count_evidence.detail: get_factors_pll_video0 at 0xffffff800845f790 executes mov x4, #0xbb and passes x4 as the entry count

pll_factor_table.encoding_observation: rows 0-13 use D2=1 only; from row 14 the table alternates D2=0 / D2=1. Both encodings yield the same rate ladder, so N and D2 must be decoded per row and are not monotonic across the table.

claimed_last_word_0x6400.verdict: interior row, 9 rows before the real end; the earlier claim that it was the final entry was a transcription error

pll_selection.set_rate: sunxi_clk_factors_set_rate at 0xffffff800845c0fc -> get_factors then register write

max_clamp.initialiser: sunxi_clk_factor_initlimits at 0xffffff800845faf0 loads [0xffffff800903deac] (the rate word of the last table entry) and stores it there; the same function seeds pllvideo1_max = 630 MHz
max_clamp.instruction: cmp w3, w0 ; csel w3, w3, w0, ls  -> min(max, request)

pll_selection.rate_quantisation: udiv by 1 000 000 truncates the request to whole MHz before the lookup
pll_selection.policy: clamp then nearest neighbour, ties resolved to the lower row; requests below the first entry map to row 0 because sunxi_clk_freq_search returns 0 when hi becomes -1

baseline_286mhz.request_origin: lcd_clk_enable: 1 x divider 11 x lcd_dclk_freq 26 MHz

hz120_572mhz.note: 576 MHz exists in the table, so the clock source is reachable at this request; the CCF lands on 576, not 572, so DCLK would be 576/11 = 52.3636 MHz

divider.high_nibble: 0xf, written by tcon0_open via orr w1, w1, #0xf0000000
divider.source: constant table 0xffffff80089f6070 indexed by lcd_if (not lcd_type), stride 0x14
divider.override_instruction: cmp w0, #0x1a ; mov w0, #0xb ; csel w1, w1, w0, ne
divider.override_condition: NE keeps the table value, EQ takes 11: exactly 26 MHz selects 11

clock_parent.driver_behavior: disp_lcd_init captures the boot parent with clk_get_parent; lcd_clk_enable re-applies the same pointer with clk_set_parent
clock_parent.active_parent_evidence: runtime clk_summary (tcon_lcd = pll_video0x4 = 288 MHz); the code only re-applies whatever it inherited
clock_parent.clk_set_rate_in_lcd_path: lcd_clk_enable issues clk_set_rate(286 MHz) then clk_get_rate; disp_lcd_init itself does not

panel.dead_field: +0x118 has no writer anywhere in the image; its only reader is gated on lcd_hv_if == 12, which the baseline does not set
panel.callbacks: cfg_panel_info / open_flow / close_flow / user_defined_func, no set_bright

input_identity.data_pointer_caveat: relocation-like pointer fields inside .kernel and .kernel2 are all zero in this ELF; clock/panel descriptor tables can therefore only be read through scalar fields or through code immediates, never by following a pointer

functions.name: calc_rate_video1
functions.result: same, but the divisor is multiplied by 4 (ubfiz #2)

functions.name: sunxi_clk_factors_recalc_rate
functions.role: extracts the factor fields from the descriptor and tail-calls the per-PLL calc
functions.result: field order n,m,p,d1,d2,frac,predictors; N at shift 8 width 8, D2 at shift 1 width 1 for PLL_VIDEO0

functions.name: get_factors_pll_video0
functions.role: target rate to factor word search

functions.name: disp_al_lcd_get_clk_info
functions.result: divider comes from a per-lcd_type constant table, not from the pixel clock

functions.name: disp_al_lcd_cfg
functions.role: programs tcon0 for the active panel
functions.result: calls tcon0_set_dclk_div(clk_info.byte4), then tcon0_cfg, tcon0_cfg_ext, tcon0_src_select

functions.name: tcon0_set_dclk_div
functions.result: bfxil into TCON base+0x44 bits[6:0]; no +/-1 and no /N adjustment in the code

functions.name: tcon0_cfg

clock_tree_conclusion.parent_fed_to_tcon_lcd: pll_video0x4 at 288 MHz (clk_summary at capture time); pll_video0 = 72 MHz is the /4 derived node, not the PLL output
clock_tree_conclusion.code_side_parent_selection: unresolved: the tcon_lcd mux/parent table is data in .kernel2 whose pointer fields are zero in this ELF, so the parent choice cannot be read statically. The runtime clk_summary is the only evidence for the parent.
clock_tree_conclusion.driver_reselects_at_runtime: not observed in this image: the only writer of TCON base+0x44 is disp_al_lcd_cfg (init path) and disp_al_vdevice_cfg (tv path); there is no runtime refresh-switch path

pll_bitfield.register: 0x03001040 (video PLL, as named in the same-boot readback report)

bits[0].meaning: not read by calc_rate_video0 for this PLL

bit31.meaning: PLL enable is the conventional bit for this CCU generation, but the enable field lives in the per-clock factors descriptor whose pointer fields are zero in this ELF, so it is not binary-confirmed

pll_bitfield.consistency: matches the measured pll_video0x4 / tcon_lcd = 288 MHz in the same boot
pll_bitfield.open_discrepancy: factor_pllvideo0x4_tbl pairs words with rates 288..336 MHz (step 6 MHz), but the same words evaluate to 576..672 MHz under calc_rate_video0, i.e. exactly 2x. The table therefore is not a usable decode oracle; only calc_rate_video0 is used above, and the 2x relation is recorded as unresolved rather than explained away.

divider_encoding.writer_semantics: val = readl(base+0x44); bfxil val, div, #0, #7; writel(val, base+0x44)
divider_encoding.field: bits[6:0] = 11, written verbatim: no minus-one, no plus-one, no log2 encoding anywhere in the writer or its caller
divider_encoding.upper_bits: bits[31:28] = 0xf are preserved by the read-modify-write and are not touched by the divider path; their meaning is unresolved

where_11_comes_from.override_that_yields_11: for lcd_type index 0, if the SoC/version word at [table_base_context+0x80] != 0x1a then the divider is forced to 0x0b = 11
where_11_comes_from.consequence: the dclk divider is a compile-time constant for the lcd_type branch, not a function of the lane pixel clock; the DT lcd_dclk_freq value never reaches this computation

panel_profile_branch.dt_property_parser: lcd_driver_name, lcd_dclk_freq, lcd_ht, lcd_vt, lcd_hbp, lcd_hspw, lcd_vbp, lcd_vspw, lcd_if, lcd_hv_if all exist as script/DT lookup keys in .kernel
panel_profile_branch.timing_source: device tree at runtime (live-fdt.json), not a static kernel panel timing table
panel_profile_branch.static_timing_table: none found: no 720/480/820/536 integer sequence exists anywhere in .kernel2, so the panel timing cannot come from the kernel image
panel_profile_branch.lcd_type: lcd_type=old reaches the divider selection through cfg->lcd_type index 0; the exact enum mapping from the bootarg string to index 0 is data-driven and not statically resolvable from this ELF
